newsitem.title: UK: London trade discounts Russian sugar buying talk.
newsitem.headline: London trade discounts Russian sugar buying talk.

text.p: Sugar brokers discounted market talk on Friday that Russia was open to buy, or had already bought, up to 100,000 tonnes of raw sugar, saying it was probably too early in the season for purchases.

While world prices are low enough at present to encourage buying and the Russian beet crop is expected to produce less sugar than last year, brokers said they were sceptical that the country would be interested in buying so much sugar so soon.
"I think they have contracts for that time of the year but they're not starting to price it yet," said one broker.
"I think they will be buying...but I don't think they've rushed into the market and bought 100,000 tonnes," she said.

Other trade sources said Russian reserves of sugar were still high and the centralised system of buying, a hangover from the former communist economy, would prevent large-scale purchases without the prior knowledge of international players.
"The warehouses are still reasonably full at the moment and the Russians still buy the way they used to," said another broker at a London trade house.
"There's nothing concrete as yet as far as we're concerned ...I'd be be surprised to find them buying so early."
Cuba would be the most likely origin for any Russian purchases, and possibly Thailand, traders said.
In its daily report, broker Merrill Lynch said Russia was more likely to make its sugar purchases later in the season when its final crop outturn was more certain.
"Recent reports have indicated smaller output in that nation (Russia) and in the Ukraine, making the reports seem plausible, especially at these lower price levels," it said.
"If true, this could be the impetus needed to put the market back up towards 11 cents."
World raw sugar prices are currently valued at just under 10.90 cents/lb for March delivery.
Analysts have forecast Russia's 1996/97 beet sugar production at 1.90 million tonnes raw value, down from last year's 2.23 million tonnes.

This week the International Sugar Organization (ISO) forecast Russian sugar consumption at 5.4 million tonnes for 1996/97 and total import demand at three million tonnes, implying stocks would be used to satisfy demand.
Last month, local trade sources said the higher Ukrainian imports had given the Russian market reserves of some 300,000 tonnes of refined sugar.
Ukraine exported around one million tonnes of sugar to Russia over the first six months of this year, 30 percent more than the same period a year ago.
But then Russia announced a 10 percent value-added tax to be slapped on all Ukrainian raw and refined sugar imports from October 1 to protect its own producers.
